_comment: Digital SAT Math blueprint (2024+ digital SAT): 44 questions, 70 minutes, multiple choice (4 choices, A-D) plus student-produced response (grid-in). Content = Fable-authored, sympy-verified items (seeds/sat-items.generated.json, source sat-fable; spec in seeds/sat-math/SAT_SPEC.md). All items are original. Delivered as the real section is: two 22-item, 35-minute modules, Module 2 routed harder or easier on Module 1 (utils/testModules.js), scored with IRT over all 44 items.
title: SAT Math Practice Test
subject: sat-math
_answerTypesComment: About 75% multiple choice, 25% grid-in on the real section. The assembler does not pace the mix; the bank's own share (101 MC / 31 grid-in = 23% grid-in) carries through the draw.
_sourcesComment: REQUIRED for this blueprint. The skills below are unified-taxonomy ids shared with the whole tutoring bank; without a source pin a SAT form would draw worksheet practice items. See utils/actTestAssembler.js bankFilter.
_structuralLookAlikesComment: SAT stems are mostly math, so the ACT-tuned word-overlap template check never fires on them: one form carried both 'If √(x + 7) = 5' and 'If √(x − 4) + 3 = 8'. With this on, a form never holds two items of one structuralSignature (utils/actTestAssembler.js) while the category has anything else. Pinned by tests/integration/satLookAlikes.test.js.
_categoryWeightsComment: College Board's published domain shares for the Math section: Algebra ~35% (13-15 of 44), Advanced Math ~35% (13-15), Problem-Solving and Data Analysis ~15% (5-7), Geometry and Trigonometry ~15% (5-7). 15/15/7/7 sums to 44. Bank depth at authoring (2026-10-07): 40/39/27/26 items, so a student gets two full forms before forms run short.
_difficultyRampComment: Bank difficulties run 2-4. One smooth easy-to-hard ramp across the form, mean 3. The real section ramps within each 22-item module; that arrives with the two-module delivery.
_modulesComment: The digital SAT Math section is two modules of 22 questions and 35 minutes each. Module 1 is the same mixed-difficulty module for everyone; Module 2 is HARDER or EASIER depending on Module 1, and once it starts Module 1 is closed. Domain counts are split across the two modules so the section still totals 15/15/7/7. The top-level categoryWeights/difficultyRamp/timeLimitMinutes describe the whole section; each module's own values are what its form is assembled from. Each route's difficultyBand is a hard floor and ceiling on every Module 2 draw, fallbacks included (utils/actTestAssembler.js difficultyBand). The ramp only centres a +/-1 window, so before the bands a harder Module 2 at target 3 drew difficulty-2 items (an f(5)-level question on the harder route) and the two routes overlapped across most of their range (QA pass, 2026-10-13). The bank is rated 2-4, so the routes still share the 3s; the ramps steer the harder route to its 4s and the easier route to its 2s within them.
_routingComment: Module 2 is harder when the Module 1 ability estimate (MAP, Rasch, bank difficulty 1-5 mapped to -3..+3 logits) is at least harderIfTheta. College Board does not publish its cut; 0 means 'did about as well as an average student on a mixed module' (roughly half right). Move it once real practice results can be compared with official scores.
_irtScaleComment: APPROXIMATE, and labelled so to the student. Scaled score = center + perLogit x theta, from the MAP ability over all 44 answers, clamped to 200-800 and rounded to 10; the likely range is theta +/- one standard error. Because the score comes from WHICH items were answered, the route is priced in: a perfect easier Module 2 after a weak Module 1 cannot reach 800. THE LINE IS SET FROM THE FORM'S OWN EXTREMES (2026-10-13): a perfect paper on the harder route (theta ~ +3.5 over these ramps) reaches 800 and a blank paper on the easier route (theta ~ -3.5) reaches 200, so center 500 and 85 per logit, and every miss in between costs points (44 -> 800, 43 -> 770, 42 -> 750, 40 -> 710, 30 -> 600 on the harder route). The previous 510 / 120 put the ceiling at theta 2.4, which a 40-of-44 paper already exceeds: 0 to 4 misses all read 800 and the likely range collapsed to a single number (external PSAT test report). A blank paper is the scale minimum (utils/testModules.js irtScaled), as on the real test. Replace with a calibrated scale once real scores can be paired with practice results.
